To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and deployed BCI seizure prediction based on deep learning and IoT to address the nonstationarity of EEG and ECo G signals and the challenges of big data in real-time applications.
the use of deep learning in conjunction with the IoT provides a means of predicting and localizing the onset of epileptic seizures from scalp EEG and/or ECoG data.
we have proposed and developed a novel BCI seizure prediction method based on the deep-learning structures of SAE and CNN, which are optimized based on PCA, ICA, and DSA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of deep learning and IoT to EEG big data for the prediction of epileptic seizures.
developing a novel deep learning method and an optimized IoT cloud computing system for BCI seizure prediction.
a BCI seizure prediction system for real-time processing of big data in a cloud computing framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a significant improvement on the state of the art and is a major step towards a real-time BCI for seizure prediction and localization.
this work has demonstrated the feasibility of a cloud computing-based BCI system to predict epileptic seizures and localize the seizure focus in a timely and efficient manner.
the proposed BCI seizure prediction system has a potential to provide a new and effective solution to patients with medically refractory epilepsy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed deep learning structures, IoT and big data are the most promising approaches for the future of BCI.

the developed BCI can be used as a new tool for the prediction of seizure onset in patients with medically refractory focal epilepsies, and the proposed method has potential to provide a new approach for the treatment of epilepsy.
the proposed BCI seizure detection and localization is the first of its kind to offer real-time processing, storage, and analysis of the preictus and ictus periods in the cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning and cloud computing are powerful tools for the analysis of large-scale EEG data.
deep-learning algorithms can be optimized for big data and can be deployed on the cloud for seizure prediction.
the IoT cloud-computing architecture can provide the required computing and storage resources to support deep learning for BCI seizure prediction from EEG and ECoGs big data.
